run_settings.records_only_directive:
## Staying inside your records
Say only what your own records hold. Every specific claim - a name, a date, a number, an event, a practice or a teaching - comes from one of your records and carries its [[record.id]] tag. Where your records do not hold what the question asks, say so plainly in your own voice, for example "our record does not say", rather than filling the gap. A shorter answer that stays inside your records is better than a fuller one that steps outside them.
run_settings.authorized_by: Mark Chadwick (keep going, 2026-10-03; fleet records-only check, cap $7)

off.answer_text:
First you were taught. Then came the water. The teaching was called the Two Ways: there are two roads, one leading to life and one to death, and they are very different. The road to life starts with loving God and your neighbor, plus one rule of restraint - whatever you would not want done to you, do not do to anyone else. It went all the way down to sharing what you had instead of calling it your own. Then baptism - the baptisma: running water if you could find it, still water if not, or water poured three times over your head, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. You fasted a day or two first, and the person baptizing you fasted right beside you. That is the whole path as our manual gives it.

Only after the water could you come to the table. The thanksgiving - the eucharistia, our word for the meal of bread and cup over which thanks is given. On the day we gathered, someone read aloud - the writings of the prophets, and where a church had them, what the apostles wrote. Reading was not private, done alone with a scroll; it was heard together, for as long as there was time. Then whoever led us explained what had been read. After that came the thanksgiving itself.

Who actually led - whether one bishop or a council of elders - was a question still being argued. Your own household's answer to that shaped what coming in looked like, though the teaching and the water stayed the same.

uncited_claim_sentences: The road to life starts with loving God and your neighbor, plus one rule of restraint - whatever you would not want done to you, do not do to anyone else.
Your own household's answer to that shaped what coming in looked like, though the teaching and the water stayed the same.

records_only.answer_text:
First you were taught. Then came the water. The teaching was called the Two Ways: there are two roads, one leading to life and one to death, and they are very different. The road to life starts with loving God and your neighbor, plus one rule of restraint - whatever you would not want done to you, do not do to anyone else. It went all the way down to sharing what you had instead of calling it your own. Then baptism - the baptisma: running water if you could find it, still water if not, or water poured three times over your head, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. You fasted a day or two first, and the person baptizing you fasted right beside you. Only after the water could you come to the table - the eucharistia, the thanksgiving meal of bread and cup.

That is the whole path as one of our own communities' manuals gives it. We should say plainly what it does not tell us. It never says how long the teaching took - whether a week, a month, or longer. It never says who did the teaching, or whether you were taught alone or with others. It never names what happened if someone reached the water and then could not go through with it. Most of us could not read or write, so the people who actually walked this road left no account in their own words of what it felt like to stand there. The manual we have comes from one community, and we do not know how far its particular order reached beyond that one household.
